scope: Proposition 5.4 of the manuscript “Existential–universal real sentences in the counting hierarchy” (preprints/Existential-universal-real-sentences-in-the-counting-hierarchy-October-4-2026/etr-counting-hierarchy.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 141 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 151fe6144a42154d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let F ∈ Z[x1, . . . , xn] be nonnegative on Rn, let n ≥ 1, and choose an odd ℓ ≥ 3 with ℓ > deg F. Define G, hu, fi, Q, D by Equations (5.1) and (5.2). Let H, V be nonnegative integers bounding log2 ∥Q∥1 and degu Q, respectively, and choose the parameters in Equation (5.7). Then q(y) = Q(U, y) is monic and squarefree, has degree D and coefficient norm at most 2K, and satisfies F has a real zero ⇐⇒ q has a real root less than R. (5.8) Every real root of q is the value of hU at a real common zero of f1(·, U), . . . , fn(·, U). When F varies in a controlled family, ℓ is chosen from its degree bound as above, and H, V are polynomial-time computable short bounds, q is controlled. All remaining bound parameters in Equation (5.7), including D, H∆, are computable in polynomial time and have polynomial binary length.
